seo.meta_description: JNTUK R23 CSE/IT 3-1 Principles of Operating Systems: processes, threads, scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, memory and file systems.
seo.title: Principles of Operating Systems - R23 3-1

Official JNTUK R23 Information Technology course structure and syllabus

source.college_source_note: JNTUK's official 2026 Open Elective-I syllabus confirms the course placement, 3-0-0-3 credits, and the same five units; the earlier official CSE and IT syllabus documents remain linked as corroborating primary sources.

units.title: Operating Systems Overview and System Structures
topics: Operating systems overview: introduction, OS functions, OS operations, computing environments, free and open-source operating systems
System structures: operating system services, user and operating-system interface, system calls and types of system calls
System programs; operating system design and implementation; operating system structure
Building and booting an operating system; operating system debugging

units.title: Processes, Threads and CPU Scheduling
topics: Processes: process concept, process scheduling, operations on processes, inter-process communication
Threads and concurrency: multithreading models, thread libraries, threading issues
CPU scheduling: basic concepts, scheduling criteria, scheduling algorithms
Multiple-processor scheduling

units.title: Process Synchronization and Deadlocks
topics: Synchronization tools: the critical section problem and Peterson's solution
Mutex locks, semaphores, monitors and classic problems of synchronization
Deadlocks: system model and deadlock characterization
Methods for handling deadlocks

units.title: Memory Management and Storage
topics: Memory-management strategies: contiguous memory allocation, paging, structure of the page table, swapping
Virtual memory management: demand paging, copy-on-write, page replacement
Allocation of frames and thrashing
Storage management: overview of mass storage structure and HDD scheduling

units.title: File Systems
topics: File system interface: file concept, access methods, directory structure
File system implementation: file-system structure and operations, directory implementation
Allocation methods and free space management
File-system internals: file-system mounting, partitions and mounting, file sharing
